question: Article 4 of Directive 2008/98/EC, as last amended by Directive (EU) 2018/851, establishes the waste hierarchy. Article 4(3) requires Member States to use economic instruments and appropriate measures to promote the application of the waste hierarchy.

Italy also has a technical standard in force, UNI 11951:2024, which establishes detailed requirements for the use of pre-consumer and post-consumer waste wood to produce wood-based materials. Among other aspects, it regulates permitted waste wood types, excluded material types, limit values for certain pollutants and requirements for the processing, quality control and testing of final products. 1.

Are there any plans or initiatives to develop an EN standard for the use of waste wood in the production of wood-based materials, and what opportunities or challenges does the Commission foresee in this regard?
In principle, to what extent does the Commission see a need for EU-wide harmonisation of technical requirements for the recycling of waste wood, and what factors would need to be considered?

What measures is the Commission considering to promote the application of the waste hierarchy and the implementation of circular economy principles in the material use of waste, while taking account of different national contexts and the need for workable and economically viable implementation for stakeholders?
answer: The Commission does not intend to develop an EU standard for the use of waste wood in the production of wood-based materials. However, assuming that the concerned waste wood falls within the scope of the Waste Framework Directive (WFD ) (1) (i.e.

, it is not exempted by Article (2)(1)(f)), Articles (5)(2) and (6)(2) enable the Commission to establish detailed criteria on the uniform application of the conditions laid down, respectively, in Articles (5)(1) or (6)(1) thereof). These are referred to respectively as end-of-waste or by-products criteria.
Such criteria have not been laid down for wood waste, following a prioritisation based on the report by the Joint Research Centre of the Commission (2).

The Circular Economy Act (3) which the Commission intends to table by 2026 will look into possible improvements in the procedures of adoption of EU-wide end-of-waste and by-product criteria to facilitate the establishment of a Single Market for secondary raw materials.

More broadly, the Commission has promoted the application of the waste hierarchy and the implementation of circular economy principles through a wide range of political and legislative initiatives, including those listed in the European Green Deal (4) and the two Circular Economy Action Plans (5).

More recently, the Commission carried out a review of WFD, adopted the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulatio n (6), and issued recommendations to Member States based on the Early Warning Reports.
